page: Microsoft Azure E8bs_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It runs on a dedicated 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The system exposes 8 virtual CPUs derived from 4 physical cores via simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and SHA_NI cryptographic extensions, backed by a 48 MB L3 cache.

Benchmark measurements across core computational tasks position the instance predominantly in the middle quartile of cloud hardware. It scores 1,616 in Geekbench single-core and 6,051 in multi-core execution, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 11,488.07 and database operations rating of 4,132.17. Memory bandwidth tests yield 57.57 GB/sec for uncached read-only transfers and 39.59 GB/sec for large block writes, allowing the instance to sustain 7.73 million Redis SET operations per second. However, compute-dense tasks show lower relative performance, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (31.6 GB/sec) and medium model 7B LLM inference falling into the lower quartile.

The instance does not include bundled local storage or attached GPUs, requiring administrators to provision remote Azure managed block storage for persistent or temporary disk capacity. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware profile prioritizes dense memory capacity and block storage throughput over raw computing scale, making it cost-effective for memory-constrained workloads without paying for surplus compute threads.

Microsoft Azure E8bs_v5 is suited for enterprise relational database servers, in-memory caching systems such as Redis, moderate transactional data stores, and backend enterprise services requiring elevated memory capacities relative to active CPU execution.
